messages.subject: [statnet_help] stepping algorithm trace values
messages.body_plain:
Hi Nicola,

I know my reply is late (and that you probably found a solution) but,
anyway, it could be useful for others...

When you download the ERGM package sources on CRAN,

http://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/contrib/r-release/ergm_2.4-3.zip

you can slightly modify the ./ergm/R/ergm.stepping.R file by
uncommenting (removing the #) line 206 and 207.

After, you have to recompile the package from these modified sources by
running in a terminal:

R CMD INSTALL ergm/

Or, inside R:

install.packages("<PATH/TO/ERGM/SOURCES>",repos=NULL)

Now, when you use the stepping algo, your ergm object will contain the
informations you need:

mymodel <- ergm(<blablabla_whith_stepping>)
mymodel$allmeanvals # give all mean value parameter estimates
mymodel$allparamvals # give all eta


Best regards,
Victorin

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Stepping algo and constraints
messages.body_plain:
Dear Statnet developers,

I think that the stepping algo, as it is coded in the ergm package
2.4-3, doesn't take into account the "contraints" argument defined in
ergm() functions (actually I need a maxout=5 constraint).

I created here some simple code to show you the problem:

#####
library(ergm)

# We simulate a network under the maxout constraint:
net <- simulate(network(50) ~ edges, theta0 = -1, constraints = ~
bd(maxout = 5))
plot(net)
max( rowSums( net[,] ) )

# model formula
f <- net ~  edges

#model estimation
m1 <- ergm(formula = f, theta0 = "MPLE", constraints = ~ bd(maxout = 5),
control = control.ergm( check.degeneracy = FALSE, style = "Stepping",
stepMCMCsize = 300, gridsize = 1000, metric = "lognormal"), burnin = 1e
+4, MCMCsamplesize = 1e+3, interval = 1e+4, maxit = 1, verbose = F )

m1$coef # BINGO, underestimation of the edge param.

# goodness of fit:
m1gof <- simulate(object = f, theta0 = m1$coef , nsim=100, burnin=1e+4,
interval=1e+4, basis = NULL, statsonly=TRUE, sequential=TRUE,
constraints = ~ bd(maxout=5), control = control.simulate.formula(),
verbose=TRUE)
plot(c(m1gof), type="l",ylim=c(150,250))
abline(a= summary(net~edges) ,b=0, col ="red")
legend("bottomright",legend=c("nb of edges in simulated networks","nb of
edges in observed network") ,fill=c("black","red") )
####

After some tests and verifications, I successfully modified the sources
as follow:

- In the "./R/ergm.R" file, change line 286:
    "Stepping" = ergm.stepping(theta0, nw, model, Clist, initialfit,
by this one:
    "Stepping" = ergm.stepping(theta0, nw, model, Clist, initialfit,
constraints,


- In the ".R/ergm.stepping.R" file, change line 39:
	ergm.stepping = function(theta0, nw, model, Clist, initialfit,
by this one:
	ergm.stepping = function(theta0, nw, model, Clist, initialfit,
constraints,

- In the ".R/ergm.stepping.R" file, change lines 69 and 161:
        interval=MCMCparams$interval, statsonly=TRUE,
by this one:
        interval=MCMCparams$interval, statsonly=TRUE,
constraints=constraints,

After recompiling the package with these small modifications, I obtain
much better results with the above example.

As, I didn't modify the simulate.ergm file, I'm pretty confident these
modifications won't affect other parts of the package.

Best regards,
Victorin Luisier

P.S: A big thank for the newly added comments in the sources, they are
very useful indeed.

--

messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] Creating weights matrices for use in sna lnam function
messages.body_plain:
Hi there

I'm trying to fit a linear autocorrelation model using the lnam
function in the sna package.

I've developed a number of possible models with different geodesic
distances, reciprocal and nonreciprocal friends. Lnam will fit a model
when the matrix order is in the correct order, but not if my variables
are ordered to match the order of the relevant person ID's in the
adjacency matrix.

The matrices are typically 647*647 node matrices with 2336 vertices.
My rownames and colnames are a list of ID numbers in the same order,
and I've checked that the one specifications match my original data.
There are no ones on the diagonal.  The matrices produce the following
response from R;

"Error in qr.solve(t(X) %*% X, t(X) %*% W1a %*% y) :  singular matrix
'a' in solve"

I've get the same response testing a variety of subsets of the matrix,
matrices with different levels of geodesic distances, alternative
covariates, alternative dependent variables, matrices transformed into
network objects.

I've been able to get these spatial error models (errorsarlm) and
spatial lag models(lagsarlm) to run in spdep which applies the same
equation and also uses maximum likelihood through "solve" to find a
solution. I was hoping to cross check a couple of the results by
running them in lnam but the inability of lnam to run these models has
made me question the equivalence of the two methods

Does anyone know of a possible solution to the singular matrix
problem? Perhaps something in the settings of lnam or a way to
transform the matrix so that it is no longer singular
(non-invertible)?


Please let me know if any additional details are needed to understand my query


Thank you in advance

Jenny Long
PhD student
University of Auckland

Jenny
I encountered a similar problem, I think, and discovered that nodes with the
same profile seemed to cause this.  Specifically, isolates are linearly
dependent and so should be removed.
If you have isolates this may be causing the problem or nodes that have
identical links.
-Tom Valente

Thanks for your prompt response and suggestions - it's nice to know other
people have run into similar difficulties!

It turned out that dummy coded categorical variables were the cause of my
singular matrix problem - I turn these into a single column and the
singular matrix issue disappears!

Your suggestions sent me on an important journey to understand more about
the identical links and isolates present in my data, so thank you very much
for your prompt reply :-)


Warm regards

Jenny Long
PhD student
University of Auckland

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Isolates in ergm
messages.body_plain:
Hi Steven and Pavel, thanks very much for the suggestion.

I posted to enquire because I have difficulty in finding a model with
satisfactory goodness-of-it (after trying multiple possible terms)
mainly owning to the preponderance of isolates.

If the isolates were included, then my follow-up question is: what is
the acceptable goodness-of-fit in ergm? Do the modellers have to
conduct an ergm regenerating the observed network 'perfectly'? If my
aim is to test the explanatory power of some generating mechanisms, is
it acceptable to demonstrating a model with certain terms generates
the observed network better than models without such terms holding all
others constant, just like the practices of ordinary OLS modelling?

Regards
Wincent

On 25 December 2011 06:32, Steven Goodreau <goodreau@uw.edu> wrote:
> Hi Wincent,
>
> To follow on with that: I agree with Pavel - you would rarely want to
> exclude isolates, and if you did, it should be because you believe that they
> are somehow excluded from the stochastic process you are modeling; I have a
> hard time coming up with a reasonable example, but if you were in that case,
> you would then need to condition your model on no isolates.
>
> Now, assuming you do include the isolates in the network for estimation --
> whether you then want to explicitly include an isolates term in the model or
> not, or consider some other set of model parameters that would address the
> preponderance of isolates (other degree terms, for instance) is really a
> question of the hypotheses that you are interested in testing. ?This is a
> substantive question that only you and your collaborators can really answer.
>
> Cheers,
> Steve
>
>
